taste.name: The construction lines stay on
taste.trigger: When a course about grids needed a page of its own
taste.decision: Chose to leave registration marks, brackets and cursor guides visible over hiding the grid once the layout was done
taste.reason: The marks give empty columns a job, so open space looks measured instead of unfinished, and the page becomes its own lesson
evidence: '+' marks on a 176px x 175px pitch, fixed while content scrolls
cc-guide-h 1440x1 and cc-guide-v 1x900 follow the pointer

taste.name: No colour of its own
taste.trigger: When framing student work that comes in every colour
taste.decision: Chose a strictly black-and-grey frame over a brand accent
taste.reason: A grey frame hands all the chroma to the work inside it, so the red and blue embeds look louder than they are
evidence: 2 background values, 3 text values, all neutral
colour appears only inside the 780x430 work embeds

taste.name: Wide grotesk speaks, mono annotates
taste.trigger: When claims and explanations had to sit side by side
taste.decision: Chose two typefaces with a hard job split over one family in several weights
taste.reason: A reader sorts statement from footnote at a glance, and mono reads like a spec sheet, which lends a paid course some rigour
evidence: RF Dewi Expanded only at 56-230px (133 nodes)
56px statements with a first-line indent of about 350px (2 grid columns)
lists as 22px hairline rows ending in [ + ]

taste.name: Content arrives out of fog
taste.trigger: When hundreds of elements needed an entrance
taste.decision: Chose one fixed blur band at the viewport's bottom edge over a fade-up timed per element
taste.reason: One global effect gives everything an entrance for free and marks the sharp zone as the reading zone
evidence: no per-element reveal on text rows
logo shrinks 100px to 20px in the first 300px of scroll and never leaves the screen
